newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes flat vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed barely moved in dull Friday trade, but the money market was fairly active, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.95 after opening at about the same level and hovering just above it for much of the day, dealers said.
"It moved within a very narrow range," a Hatton National Bank dealer said. "There were people who were willing to buy, but their demand was not that big."
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by two local cents. Buying and selling prices were at 56.3112 and 57.4488.
Overnight call money closed at 14.5 percent after opening at 15.
"One bank got stuck for money and as a result the market panicked and rates shot up to 17 percent. But once the requirement was satisfied, rates came down again," the Hatton National dealer said.

Other dealers said volatility in call money is expected to ease, with the coming into effect on Friday of the new statutory reserve requirement of 14 percent against 15, which is expected to release about four billion rupees into the system.
